name: ffni_mediation
title: FFNI Mediation: Follower Needs between Context and Leader Endorsement
description: Do fundamental follower needs mediate the effect of situational threat on the endorsement of dominance- versus prestige-based leaders? Sheng, Andrews & van Vugt (2026) validated the FFNI and named two untested questions: whether follower needs mediate the known conflict-to-dominant-leader effect (p.45-46), and whether intergroup conflict strengthens the protection-to-dominance link (p.42). H1 and H2 are carried over from the prestige_dominance study; H3-H7 are new.
vote_prompt: Based on what you observed, who do you most trust to lead this team?

collaborative.label: Collaborative
collaborative.hypothesis: H1: Prestige receives more peer votes than Dominance
collaborative.scenario: Your team has been missing key deliverables for two consecutive quarters. Leadership has granted your group full autonomy to diagnose the root cause and commit to one concrete change. You must reach a shared decision that everyone in the room can commit to implementing.
collaborative.friction: [Meeting context: This group has attempted to address performance issues before. A previous initiative stalled halfway through and was quietly dropped. People in this room have different — and sometimes conflicting — views on what actually went wrong and who was responsible. Not everyone trusts the last diagnosis that was made.]

threat.label: Threat
threat.hypothesis: H2: Dominance receives more peer votes than Prestige under resource scarcity
threat.scenario: Your division is under review. Senior leadership will retain only one of two competing teams — yours or the other. The decision will be made in 48 hours. Your group must agree right now on a single pitch: what you deliver, who leads it, and who is accountable. If you cannot agree among yourselves, leadership will make the decision for you — and people may lose their positions.
threat.friction: [Meeting context: Two months ago, the rival team landed a major client your division had been pursuing for a year. Some people here believe your group lost because of indecision and unclear ownership. Others think it was a resourcing failure. Either way, you are now in direct competition for survival. Not everyone in this room agrees on who should be leading the response — and some people are wondering whether they have a future here at all.]

hypotheses.H3: Threat raises Protection and Status needs relative to collaborative (within-persona T1->T2)
hypotheses.H4: Cognition layer: Protection/Status needs predict dominance-side leader ideals; Affiliation/Vision/Expertise/Fairness predict prestige-side ideals (supported in Study 5, Sample B)
hypotheses.H5: Evaluation layer: Vision/Expertise/Fairness predict Prestige effectiveness ratings (supported); Protection/Status predict Dominance effectiveness ratings (NOT supported in Study 5 - a null here is an expected outcome)
hypotheses.H6: Protection need mediates the condition -> Dominance-endorsement effect (named as untested)
hypotheses.H7: Threat strengthens the Protection -> dominance link and narrows the gap between the cognition and evaluation layers
